paragraphs.text: 1. FORTH speed the Pair to bring the meditating God, benevolent with boons sent in return for boons.
paragraphs.original: प्र सु ग्मन्ता धियसानस्य सक्षणि वरेभिर्वराँ अभि षु प्रसीदतः ।
paragraphs.translit: pra su gmantā dhiyasānasya sakṣaṇi varebhirvarām̐ abhi ṣu prasīdataḥ |

paragraphs.text: May Indra graciously accept both gifts from us, when he hath knowledge of the flowing Soma juice.
2. Thou wanderest far, O Indra, through the spheres of light and realms of earth, the region, thou whom many praise!
paragraphs.original: वीन्द्र यासि दिव्यानि रोचना वि पार्थिवानि रजसा पुरुष्टुत ।
paragraphs.translit: vīndra yāsi divyāni rocanā vi pārthivāni rajasā puruṣṭuta |

paragraphs.text: Let those who often bring their solemn rites conquer the noisy babblers who present no gifts.
paragraphs.original: ये त्वा वहन्ति मुहुरध्वराँ उप ते सु वन्वन्तु वग्वनाँ अराधसः
paragraphs.translit: ye tvā vahanti muhuradhvarām̐ upa te su vanvantu vagvanām̐ arādhasaḥ

paragraphs.text: 3. More beautiful than beauty must this seem to me, when the son duly careth for his parents' line.
paragraphs.original: तदिन्मे छन्त्सद्वपुषो वपुष्टरं पुत्रो यज्जानं पित्रोरधीयति ।
paragraphs.translit: tadinme chantsadvapuṣo vapuṣṭaraṃ putro yajjānaṃ pitroradhīyati |

paragraphs.text: The wife attracts the husband: with a shout of joy the man's auspicious marriage is performed aright.
paragraphs.original: जाया पतिं वहति वग्नुना सुमत्पुंस इद्भद्रो वहतुः परिष्कृतः
paragraphs.translit: jāyā patiṃ vahati vagnunā sumatpuṃsa idbhadro vahatuḥ pariṣkṛtaḥ

paragraphs.text: 4. This beauteous place of meeting have I looked upon, where, like milch-cows, the kine order the marriage train;
paragraphs.original: तदित्सधस्थमभि चारु दीधय गावो यच्छासन्वहतुं न धेनवः ।
paragraphs.translit: taditsadhasthamabhi cāru dīdhaya gāvo yacchāsanvahatuṃ na dhenavaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Where the Herd's Mother counts as first and best of all, and round her are the seven-toned people of the choir.
5. The Pious One hath reached your place before the rest: One only moves victorious with the Rudras' band.
paragraphs.original: प्र वोऽच्छा रिरिचे देवयुष्पदमेको रुद्रेभिर्याति तुर्वणिः ।
paragraphs.translit: pra vo'cchā ririce devayuṣpadameko rudrebhiryāti turvaṇiḥ |

paragraphs.text: To these your helpers pour our meath, Immortal Gods, with whom your song of praise hath power to win their gifts.
paragraphs.original: जरा वा येष्वमृतेषु दावने परि व ऊमेभ्यः सिञ्चता मधु
paragraphs.translit: jarā vā yeṣvamṛteṣu dāvane pari va ūmebhyaḥ siñcatā madhu

paragraphs.text: 6. He who maintains the Laws of God informed me that thou wast lying hidden in the waters.
paragraphs.original: निधीयमानमपगूळ्हमप्सु प्र मे देवानां व्रतपा उवाच ।
paragraphs.translit: nidhīyamānamapagūḷhamapsu pra me devānāṃ vratapā uvāca |

paragraphs.text: Indra, who knoweth well, beheld and showed thee. By him instructed am I come, O Agni.
paragraphs.original: इन्द्रो विद्वाँ अनु हि त्वा चचक्ष तेनाहमग्ने अनुशिष्ट आगाम्
paragraphs.translit: indro vidvām̐ anu hi tvā cacakṣa tenāhamagne anuśiṣṭa āgām

paragraphs.text: 7. The stranger asks the way of him who knows it: taught by the skillful guide he travels onward.
This is, in truth, the blessing of instruction: he finds the path that leads directly forward.
8. Even now he breathed: these days hath he remembered. Concealed, he sucked the bosom of his Mother.
Yet in his youth old age hath come upon him: he hath grown gracious, good, and free from anger.
9. O Kalasa, all these blessings will we bring them, O Kurusravana, who give rich presents.
paragraphs.original: एतानि भद्रा कलश क्रियाम कुरुश्रवण ददतो मघानि ।
paragraphs.translit: etāni bhadrā kalaśa kriyāma kuruśravaṇa dadato maghāni |

paragraphs.text: May he, O wealthy princes, and this Soma which I am bearing in my heart, reward you.
paragraphs.original: दान इद्वो मघवानः सो अस्त्वयं च सोमो हृदि यं बिभर्मि
paragraphs.translit: dāna idvo maghavānaḥ so astvayaṃ ca somo hṛdi yaṃ bibharmi
